source_text: Per opus Dei opus diaboli transire non sinitur. Non potest mali radix in dono Dei locari. Rerum ratio non sinit, ut de bono malum, et de iusto iniquum aliquid proferatur. Non nascuntur peccata de ea re, quae libera est a peccato. De hoc opere quod non habet culpam, nasci culpa non potest
pass_a_gloss: Through work of-God work of-the-devil to-pass not is-allowed. not is-able of-evil root in dono of-God to-be-placed. Rerum reason not allows, so-that/as about/from to-good evil, and about/from from-the-just unjust-thing something be-brought-forth. not are-born sins about/from she/it re, which free is from by-sin. about/from this by-work that/which not has fault, to-be-born fault not is-able.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere

pass_b_english: The devil’s work is not allowed to pass through God’s work.
The root of evil cannot be placed in God’s gift.
The order of things does not allow evil to be produced from good, or anything unjust from what is just.
Sins are not born from something free from sin.
Guilt cannot be born from this work, which has no guilt.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
